nodes.description: Biallelic pathogenic variants in GM2A abolish or impair the GM2 activator protein (GM2AP), a non-enzymatic lysosomal lipid-transfer cofactor required to solubilize membrane-bound GM2 ganglioside and present it to beta-hexosaminidase A. Unlike HEXA (Tay-Sachs) and HEXB (Sandhoff) deficiencies, beta-hexosaminidase A and B catalytic proteins remain intact.

nodes.description: Single-knockout Gm2a-/- mice lack GM2 activator protein and accumulate moderate brain GM2 ganglioside with mild behavioral/motor deficits and a normal lifespan (~92 weeks), modeling mild adult-onset rather than acute infantile human disease because murine neuraminidase 3 (NEU3) mediates an alternative sialidase-dependent GM2 degradation bypass.

evidence.reference_title: Characterization of a phenotypically severe animal model for human AB-Variant GM2 gangliosidosis.
evidence.snippet: Gm2a-/- mice are commonly used as a model of ABGM2. These mice are characterized by phenotypes most representative of predicted adult-onset form of ABGM2, which include moderate GM2 accumulation and mild neurological defects. This mild phenotype has been attributed to compensation by alternative GM2 degradation pathways mediated by sialidase, neuraminidase 3 (NEU3), a pathway that is more prominent in mice than humans.

nodes.description: Double-knockout Gm2a-/-Neu3-/- mice ablating both Gm2a and the compensatory murine Neu3 sialidase bypass accumulate 3- to 4-fold more brain GM2 ganglioside than Gm2a-/- mice and develop progressive tremor, ataxic gait, impaired rotarod coordination and locomotion, weight loss, widespread CNS vacuolization, and shortened survival averaging 27 weeks.

evidence.reference_title: Characterization of a phenotypically severe animal model for human AB-Variant GM2 gangliosidosis.
evidence.snippet: Double knockout mice lived an average of 27.0 ± 1.5 (mean ± SD) weeks, compared to Gm2a−/− mice, which lived a relatively normal lifespan that averaged 91.9 ± 9.8 weeks.

nodes.description: Preclinical intrathecal self-complementary AAV9 gene replacement therapy (scAAV9.hGM2A) delivering a functional human GM2A transgene achieved widespread central nervous system transduction and dose-dependent biochemical reduction of brain GM2 ganglioside storage in Gm2a-/- mice without significant chronic toxicity; human clinical trials for GM2A have not yet been initiated (clinical GM2 gene therapy trials such as TSHA-101 and AXO-AAV-GM2 target HEXA/HEXB rather than GM2A).

evidence.reference_title: Biochemical Correction of GM2 Ganglioside Accumulation in AB-Variant GM2 Gangliosidosis.
evidence.snippet: In this study, we show that intrathecal delivery of self-complementary adeno-associated virus serotype-9 (scAAV9) harbouring a functional human GM2A transgene (scAAV9.hGM2A) can prevent GM2 accumulation in in GM2AP-deficient mice (Gm2a-/- mice).

evidence.reference_title: Biochemical Correction of GM2 Ganglioside Accumulation in AB-Variant GM2 Gangliosidosis.
evidence.snippet: Taken together, these data provide proof-of-principle that scAAV9.hGM2A can stably deliver human GM2A transgene to the brain when administered intrathecally, and biochemically reduce GM2 accumulation associated with loss of function of GM2AP in a mouse model of ABGM2.

nodes.description: No disease-modifying therapy is approved for GM2 activator deficiency; management is multidisciplinary and supportive, focusing on adequate nutrition and hydration, airway protection and positioning to prevent aspiration during feedings, infection management, periodic multidisciplinary surveillance, and antiseizure therapy titrated to avoid excessive sedation.

evidence.reference_title: GM2 Activator Deficiency.
